newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA DENT INTER'S EUROPEAN CUP AMBITIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA DENT INTER'S EUROPEAN CUP AMBITIONS.

text.p: Parma striker Enrico Chiesa dented Inter's hopes of a place in the Champions' League next season while European Cup holders Juventus beat Roma to stay five points clear at the top of serie A on Saturday.

The matches, brought forward a day because of European matches next week, changed nothing as far as the top three placings in the Italian league were concerned but Parma's 1-0 home victory over Inter clarified matters.
Chiesa's 22nd-minute goal, a twist followed by an unstoppable left-footer, established Parma as the clear second force in Italy with Juventus still a cut above.

Juventus, who won 3-0 in Turin thanks to two goals from stand-in striker Christian Vieri, have 48 points while Parma, who finished with 10 men after midfielder Dino Baggio was sent off in the 79th minute for two bookings, have 43.
Inter have 38 and as much chance of finishing second, and thereby clinching a European Cup place, as Parma do of overtaking Juventus and winning the title.
AC Milan, struggling in 12th place before Saturday's match, overcame Cup Winners' Cup hopefuls Fiorentina 2-0 to leapfrog over them, Napoli and Lazio and move up to ninth.

French international midfielder Marcel Desailly headed in the first in the 61st minute from close range. Second-half substitute Demetrio Albertini scored the second with an 89th-minute penalty after George Weah was felled.
"We have rediscovered our Milan, the Milan we always want to see," said joyful club owner Silvio Berlusconi, who called his team's performance "splendid and superlative".
"Let's hope its not a one-off but I don't think so because I saw the whole team well concentrated."

Vieri, the main target man of a below-strength Juventus, scored in the 28th and 44th minutes to dismiss any notion that the absence of injured striker Alessandro del Piero and suspended Croat Alen Boksic had weakened the leaders.

The first goal was a low, rasping shot past surprised goalkeeper Giovanni Cervone after Nicola Amoruso fed the ball through. The second was worthy of the boy wonder Del Piero himself, a neat diagonal loop into the net.
Amoruso made it 3-0 in the 85th minute when Michele Padovano, brought on as a second-half substitute, missed a sitting chance but made amends by setting up his team mate.

Vieri's goals will have given the scouts from Rosenborg little encouragement since he was also the scorer of a lightning equaliser in the 1-1 European Cup quarter-final first leg draw against the Norwegian club in Trondheim.
Juventus fans have no doubts that they will be following their team into the Champions' League next season and Saturday's result at the Stadio delle Alpi reinforced that.
But the venue also added to a sense of unease, with fans unsure where they will be watching Juventus when Italian soccer's "Old Lady" celebrates her 100th anniversary this year.
The club is locked in a dispute with the city authorities over rents on the cavernous delle Alpi stadium.

Newspapers have reported that the club's officials want to stay in Turin but have already made contingency plans by approaching Reggiana to play league matches at their Reggio Emilia ground and cup matches at Milan's San Siro.
A showdown is forecast for the coming week.

Ironically, while the procession to a record 24th league "scudetto" (title shield) continues at a stately pace, the next few days could have more of an impact on the club's supporters than anything thrown at them over the past century.
